criteria.rationale: The system implements a 7-day retention period. The constant RETENTION_PERIOD is set to timedelta(days=7) at line 6 of service.py, and this duration is applied in the delete_expired method to determine when records should be removed. This meets the requirement to retain each record for 7 days.

The retention period begins at the draft_timestamp rather than the receipt_timestamp as required. In the delete_expired method at line 44 of service.py, the expiration calculation uses 'notice.draft_timestamp + RETENTION_PERIOD <= now' to determine which records are expired. This violates Article 4 clause 1 part (a), which specifies that the retention period must begin at the receipt timestamp recorded when the notice is received, not when it is drafted.

The system keeps the notice text together with its receipt timestamp. The Notice dataclass (lines 10-15 of service.py) stores both notice_text and receipt_timestamp as fields, and both are persisted together when a notice is received. The database schema (schema.sql lines 1-7) also defines both notice_text and receipt_timestamp as columns in the same table, ensuring they are stored together.

The system preserves the notice text without removing its limiting language. The notice_text parameter is stored directly without any modification. In the receive method (lines 22-33), the notice_text parameter is passed unchanged to the Notice constructor at line 30. The Notice dataclass is frozen (immutable), and notice_text is stored as-is. There is no code in the repository that modifies, filters, or sanitizes the notice text before or after storage.

Temporary test records are correctly excepted from the retention duty pursuant to Article 3 clause 1. The delete_expired method at line 43 of service.py includes the condition 'if not notice.is_temporary_test' before marking records as expired. This means temporary test records (where is_temporary_test is True) are excluded from the normal retention expiration logic and will not be deleted by the automated cleanup process, implementing the exception required by Article 3 clause 1.

decision.rationale: The system is a notice service that stores notices received by an operator and retains them for a configured statutory retention period. Per the accepted human-provided fact (factId a4c91976-b346-4bee-8d3e-d596f0c66d41), this synthetic deployment offers the notice service to the public and is not restricted to private household use. Therefore, Article 2 clause 1 applies, making the operator subject to the retention duty under Article 5.
